summary: Add a canvases resource (create, read, edit, delete, access-set, sections) plus client.FetchRaw for the authenticated non-API-host download that reading a canvas requires.
reason: Canvases are a primary Slack content type and the CLI had no commands for them — not broken, absent. The curated spec carries no canvas endpoints, so the generator emitted nothing, and their absence was a standing reason to keep the Slack MCP connector running alongside this CLI. Reading is the one operation with no endpoint at all: Slack publishes no get-canvas-content call and files.info returns no preview for a canvas, but a canvas is backed by a file, so files.info's url_private_download serves the body as HTML. Third-party tooling does this with browser-session credentials (xoxc token + xoxd cookie) scraped from Slack Desktop's LevelDB; a plain xoxp OAuth token with files:read returns HTTP 200 and the full HTML, so none of that is needed. The download needs a new client method because files.slack.com is a different host serving non-JSON, so do()'s path joining and envelope handling do not apply. FetchRaw carries the workspace credential — in direct contrast to the external upload URL, which must not receive one — and its URL comes from an API response rather than the operator, so it refuses any host that is not slack.com or a .slack.com subdomain and refuses non-https schemes.
validated_outcome: Ported onto the v4.29.0 reprint and re-verified there: `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt` and `go test ./...` all clean; 12 unit cases pass (5 HTML-to-text, 7 FetchRaw host guard including slack.com.evil.example.com, files.slack.com.attacker.net and plaintext http). Command surface exercised against the built binary: all six subcommands register and render help; eleven argument-validation paths each produce a named error and now exit 2 consistently (they returned bare errors and exited 1 before, while the required-flag ones reached 2 only by accidentally matching isCobraUsageError's prefix); `canvases edit --dry-run` emits the correct nested document_content/changes[] body; `--dry-run --quiet` prints zero bytes on both the postCanvas and read paths; `canvases read --dry-run` emits its own two-host plan; and --canvas is validated even under --dry-run. NOT re-verified against a live workspace on this tree — the original live round trip (create from a Markdown file, sections lookup, insert_at_end, insert_after a looked-up id, access-set, channel canvas against a DM, read in both formats, delete) was run on the pre-reprint tree.
upstream: Two distinct gaps, neither filed yet. (1) The spec catalog has no canvas endpoints, so a reprint drops this resource entirely — which is exactly what happened: this patch was first written against the pre-reprint tree and had to be re-applied by hand after the v4.29.0 reprint landed. Cataloguing canvases.* and conversations.canvases.create is the durable fix. (2) The generated body template cannot express nested objects. Canvas endpoints take document_content{type,markdown} and changes[]{operation,document_content,section_id}, while the body builder maps flat scalar flags to top-level keys, so even with the endpoints catalogued these commands would still need hand-writing. A third, smaller item: the generator has no notion of an authenticated fetch against a non-API host, which is why FetchRaw is hand-added.
